questions.explanation: The FAQ requires separate itemization and advance information about all charges.
feedback: An unexplained total omits the stated detail.
Disclosure occurs before the act.
Correct. Provide the required written documentation too.
The customer is the signer.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary discloses charges orally in advance but never provides a written fee list for a nonexempt paid service. What is missing?
options: Only the customer's signature on an envelope
Written documentation of the charged notarial and associated services
questions.explanation: Advance information and the written listing are separate requirements.
feedback: Another statement does not supply the required document.
A generic post is not this service's fee record.
An envelope signature does not list charges.
Correct. Supply an acceptable written fee record.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary's invoice lists separate notarial and travel amounts. Is an itemized invoice an accepted written fee format?
options: Yes, it is among the listed formats
No, only a court judgment qualifies
Only a handwritten postcard is permitted
Only a cash-register tape with no details qualifies
questions.explanation: The FAQ lists an itemized invoice among acceptable fee records.
feedback: Correct. Ensure the actual charges are clear.
A judgment is not the required ordinary documentation.
The FAQ allows several formats.
An unexplained tape may omit required detail.

questions.stem: A Colorado closing statement clearly lists the notarial charge. Which documentation conclusion follows?
options: A second commercial receipt is always mandatory
A closing statement may provide the required fee record
Closing statements can never show notarial fees
Only the stamp itself can document charges
questions.explanation: The FAQ identifies a closing statement as an acceptable written format.
feedback: The FAQ permits the stated format.
Correct. It must identify the actual applicable charge.
The FAQ lists it expressly.
A stamp is not a fee list.

questions.stem: A Colorado title-company employee performs qualifying closing services as part of the company's business. Which fee-documentation exception may apply?
options: Every independent contractor is exempt too
questions.explanation: The FAQ and Rule 2.4.3 identify the defined employee/title-service exception.
feedback: The exception distinguishes employees from contractors.
It is limited to the stated services and role.
Correct. Confirm the actual conditions.
The exception is not based simply on RON.

questions.stem: An independent Colorado signing contractor wants to use the title-company employee documentation exception solely because the client is a title company. What distinction controls?
options: Employment status and the exception's stated service conditions
questions.explanation: The FAQ expressly separates the employee exception from independent contractors.
feedback: Branding does not establish employment.
Document count does not create the exception.
Transport is unrelated.
Correct. Apply the contractor's actual documentation duties.

questions.stem: A Colorado contractor's own disclosed charge differs from what the title company ultimately charges the signer. What does the FAQ require the contractor to document?
options: The contractor's own notarial and associated charges
Only the customer's total loan balance
questions.explanation: The FAQ says the contractor is responsible for documenting the contractor's own standard charges.
feedback: Correct. Questions about the company's charges go to the company.
The contractor should not invent another business's figures.
That exceeds the described fee record.
Loan balance does not identify the contractor's charges.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary provides all notarial and associated services free. What fee-documentation requirement does the FAQ state?
options: A paid receipt must be invented
No charge documentation is required for entirely free services
A $15 receipt must always be issued
Only a bank balance printout qualifies
questions.explanation: The FAQ says no documentation is required when neither category is charged.
feedback: A false paid receipt would misstate the service.
Correct. The journal still records the actual act.
The notary need not invent a charge.
A bank balance is unrelated.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary charges no notarial fee but charges ordinary photocopying at the same appointment. What does the FAQ generally require?
options: No record because the notarial charge is zero
questions.explanation: Zero notarial price does not generally erase documentation for charged associated services.
feedback: The photocopy charge remains relevant.
An employer notice is not the customer fee record.
Correct. Apply any stated separate signing-service exception only where it fits.
Qualification does not document the charge.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary tells a closing company the charge but never informs the signer. Who does the FAQ define as the customer for fee documentation?
questions.explanation: The fee FAQ identifies the signer as the customer.
feedback: The state is not this service's customer.
The lender does not automatically replace the signer.
Ownership does not define this customer.
Correct. Provide the appropriate information to the signer.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary omits a required itemized document and says the state must assume the fee was lawful. What presumption does Rule 2.4.2 describe?
options: The notarial charge is presumed above the statutory limit
questions.explanation: The rule gives that presumption when the required specific notarial charge is not itemized.
feedback: Correct. Supply the required fee record.
The rule does not presume a zero charge.
A documentation failure does not extend office.
The rule does not transfer all payment to vendors.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary provides written fee documentation immediately after signing. What timing does Rule 2.4.1(b) permit?
options: Before the act, at signing or immediately afterward
Only before the client enters the building
questions.explanation: The rule allows those stated written-document timings while requiring advance charge information.
feedback: Thirty days later is outside the stated timing.
Correct. Distinguish written delivery from advance disclosure.
Renewal is unrelated.
The rule provides a broader practical timing choice.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary refuses to explain an additional travel amount before acting. Which Rule 2.4.1 requirement applies?
options: Only the final file size matters
Inform the customer of notarial and additional charges beforehand
Only disclose to the employer afterward
questions.explanation: The rule requires advance information verbally or in writing.
feedback: Equipment identity does not satisfy fee disclosure.
File size does not determine the duty.
Correct. Explain actual charges before the act.
Employer-only later notice misses the requirement.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary calls a required oath a separate notarial service surcharge on the same ordinary document to exceed the ordinary maximum. What does the FAQ clarify?
options: Any new label creates a new maximum
Only the client chooses the cap
All sworn acts have unlimited fees
The applicable oath is included in the ordinary document notarization fee
questions.explanation: The fee FAQ includes the required oath/affirmation among the capped act components.
feedback: Labels cannot remove the included component.
The state sets the applicable maximum.
The FAQ supplies a limit.
Correct. Apply the cap to the actual service.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary wants to show fee information on a business card that actually lists the charged fees. Is that format recognized?
options: Yes, the FAQ lists a business card with fees among acceptable formats
No written cards are ever accepted
Only a bound legal opinion qualifies
Only a stamp purchase invoice qualifies
questions.explanation: The FAQ lists a fee-bearing business card as one acceptable written format.
feedback: Correct. Ensure it clearly documents the applicable charges.
The FAQ expressly recognizes the format.
A legal opinion is not the routine requirement.
A supplier invoice concerns another transaction.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary has an ordinary paper-document appointment and wants the remote $25 maximum simply because scheduling was online. What determines the category?
options: The actual notarial method and service
The cost of the notary's phone
questions.explanation: The higher listed maximum belongs to electronic or remote notarization, not online scheduling alone.
feedback: Booking does not make a paper act electronic.
Correct. Apply the ordinary cap to an ordinary paper act.
Email does not establish the performed method.
Phone price does not determine the act.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary sees old educational material listing lower fee limits than the current official fee FAQ. Which source treatment is appropriate?
options: Use the current official fee notice while checking the applicable service
questions.explanation: The current official FAQ states $15 ordinary and $25 electronic/remote maximums.
feedback: Old material may have been superseded.
Another state's limits do not govern Colorado.
Correct. Preserve the act-category distinctions.
A midpoint has no legal basis.

questions.stem: A Colorado ordinary commission is active, but the notary has not received remote approval. When may RON begin?
options: After the separate remote qualification and state approval
questions.explanation: Remote acts require an active commission and approved remote status.
feedback: Hardware does not grant authority.
Correct. Complete the state process.
Advertising is not authorization.
A customer cannot approve the public office.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote renewal is approaching. What does Rule 5.2.1(d) require within ninety days before renewal?
options: Renewal training, the required exam and fee
questions.explanation: The remote renewal rule requires timely training, testing and payment.
feedback: Correct. Ordinary renewal and remote status require the applicable steps.
An old signature does not satisfy education.
A survey is not the required course.
The rule expressly requires renewal education and examination.

questions.stem: A new Colorado applicant files remote intent with the initial application. What must occur before the first remote act?
questions.explanation: Rule 5.2.1 permits early intent filing but requires actual commissioning and approval before remote work.
feedback: Intent alone does not confer authority.
A vendor cannot approve the commission.
Correct. Wait for both public-authority conditions.
Equipment purchase is insufficient.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote notary wants several approved platforms. What minimum provider record does the FAQ require?
options: One platform can never be changed
At least one approved provider on record
questions.explanation: The FAQ allows multiple providers but requires at least one on record.
feedback: Provider information is required.
A personal app is not the approved route.
The FAQ permits more than one.
Correct. Keep the relevant state record current.

questions.stem: A Colorado vendor's software can stream video but the vendor is absent from the approved-provider list. What must be checked before use?
options: State provider approval and required recording/storage compliance
Only the vendor's number of followers
questions.explanation: The FAQ requires approved providers and compliant technology.
feedback: Correct. Functional video alone does not establish approval.
Popularity is not approval.
Camera resolution is only one aspect.
Customers do not authorize vendors for the state.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote signer agrees to video communication but refuses recording. What should the notary do?
options: Do not perform the remote act under that refusal
Have the provider delete everything immediately
questions.explanation: The remote FAQ prohibits proceeding if the signer will not agree to recording.
feedback: Recording is required.
Correct. Explain the authorized alternatives.
A screenshot is not the required recording.
Immediate deletion defeats retention.

questions.stem: Before a Colorado RON recording begins, which storage information must be disclosed?
options: Where and how long the recording will be stored
questions.explanation: The FAQ requires recording and storage details before express consent.
feedback: A phone number does not describe storage.
Commute is unrelated.
Correct. Obtain the required verbal agreement.
Employer identity does not answer storage conditions.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote signer remains silent when asked about recording and storage. What consent does the FAQ require?
options: The appearing signer's express verbal agreement
questions.explanation: The FAQ calls for express consent to both recording and storage.
feedback: The stated requirement is express agreement.
Advertising is not this signer's consent.
Another person cannot supply the customer's agreement.
Correct. Obtain and preserve the required consent.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote notary plans to retain the audio-video record for one commission year. What retention period does the FAQ state?
questions.explanation: The remote FAQ requires secure storage of the recording for ten years.
feedback: Correct. Plan suitable continuing storage.
One month is too short.
Payment does not end retention.
A later act does not erase the duty.

questions.stem: A Colorado RON recording includes only the final seal application and omits the prior interaction. What does the FAQ require?
options: Record the entire interaction including the remote notarization
Only an image of the stamp
questions.explanation: The FAQ says the entire interaction and act must be recorded.
feedback: A facial image alone does not record the procedure.
Correct. Capture the prescribed events and statements.
A price quote is not the whole act.
A stamp image omits the interaction.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary relies on personal knowledge of a remote signer. Which statement belongs in the recording?
options: How the notary knows the signer and for how long
questions.explanation: The FAQ requires explaining the personal-knowledge connection and duration.
feedback: Software choice does not establish knowledge.
The vague statement omits required detail.
Correct. Record the actual relationship.
Loan size is unrelated.

questions.stem: A Colorado credible witness identifies a remote signer. What must the witness explain in the recording?
options: How the witness knows the remotely located individual
questions.explanation: The FAQ requires the witness's knowledge explanation and the notary's own relationship explanation.
feedback: Price does not establish knowledge.
Hardware is unrelated.
A preferred date does not identify the person.
Correct. Follow the complete witness statements.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote credential route uses an ID with a photograph but no signature. What distinction matters?
options: The stated remote credential route requires photograph and signature
Ordinary photo-or-signature language automatically replaces RON rules
questions.explanation: The remote FAQ describes government ID containing both features for that route.
feedback: Correct. Apply the complete remote identity process.
The routes have different requirements.
A nickname is not the described evidence.
Payment does not establish identity.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote credential is presented but no credential analysis or required additional identity method occurs. What is missing?
options: The complete prescribed remote identification process
questions.explanation: The FAQ's route combines remote presentation, credential analysis and a stated additional method.
feedback: Contact information does not supply identity analysis.
Correct. Presentation alone is incomplete.
A paper copy does not replace the remote safeguards.
Display size does not complete the route.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary is abroad and offers a remote appointment for a Denver client. What location rule applies?
options: Only the client must be in Colorado
Any notary location is allowed with consent
The notary must be physically in Colorado
An old Colorado address is enough
questions.explanation: The remote notary must remain within Colorado borders during the act.
feedback: Client location does not cure the officer's absence.
Consent cannot waive territory.
Correct. Do not perform this Colorado RON act abroad.
An address does not establish physical presence.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote signer is outside the United States and the document concerns only unrelated foreign property. Which required connection is absent?
options: The specified United States matter, property or substantial transaction connection
questions.explanation: The outside-US route requires one of the listed US connections.
feedback: Hardware does not supply transaction nexus.
Camera choice is unrelated.
A receipt does not establish the required subject connection.
Correct. Evaluate the full foreign-signer conditions.

questions.stem: A remote signer outside the United States presents a transaction substantially connected with the US, but the Colorado notary actually knows the act is prohibited where the signer is. What follows?
options: The prohibition defeats the stated foreign-signer condition
A US connection overrides every foreign prohibition
Only a higher fee is needed
The client may waive actual knowledge
questions.explanation: The outside-US route requires no actual knowledge of prohibition in the signer's jurisdiction.
feedback: Correct. Both stated conditions must be satisfied.
The FAQ requires both conditions.
Price cannot remove the prohibition.
Consent does not change the notary's actual knowledge.

questions.stem: A Colorado election campaign requests remote notarization of a circulator affidavit for a candidate petition. What does the FAQ say?
options: All election documents are ordinary RON records
Records relating to the electoral process are excluded from RON
Only the signature's ink color matters
The campaign can approve an exception
questions.explanation: The FAQ expressly excludes these electoral-process records.
feedback: The page gives a specific exclusion.
Correct. Do not use RON for the excluded record.
Ink does not remove the subject restriction.
A campaign cannot waive the state restriction.

questions.stem: A Colorado client wants every will notarized remotely under the general RON permission. What does the FAQ require recognizing?
options: Special will/codicil restrictions and the specific electronic-wills exception
questions.explanation: The page directs special statutory restrictions for wills and codicils.
feedback: The FAQ does not give blanket permission.
Document type can determine eligibility.
Correct. Use the specific applicable statutory route.
Typography does not resolve testamentary requirements.

questions.stem: A Colorado client asks whether an ordinary qualifying real-estate deed must always be remotely notarized. What does the FAQ state?
options: RON is compulsory for every deed
Only foreign notaries may notarize deeds
Remote notarization may be used but is not required
questions.explanation: The FAQ permits qualifying real-estate RON without making it compulsory.
feedback: The FAQ expressly says it is not required.
Foreign authority is not the stated rule.
In-person lawful methods remain possible.
Correct. Select a lawful method appropriate to the transaction.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote certificate omits any indication of audio-video technology. What must be added?
questions.explanation: The remote certificate must indicate use of audio-video technology.
feedback: Correct. Use an authorized certificate with the added method statement.
Advertising does not describe the performed method.
An internal number is not the required statement.
An email does not identify the statutory remote method.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote notary uses a digitized signature that differs from the current official signature record. What should it match?
options: The official signature in the latest affirmation or later signature-change record
questions.explanation: The remote signature must exactly match the official record described by the FAQ.
feedback: A sample is not the notary's official identity.
Correct. Use the current record basis.
The notary does not sign as the customer.
The commission is individual.

questions.stem: A Colorado remote seal has a different notary ID from the ordinary wet stamp. What should the remote seal do?
options: Replace the notary's name with a URL
Exactly match the wet stamp's required identity
questions.explanation: The FAQ says the remote seal should exactly match the wet stamp.
feedback: Provider accounts do not replace public identifiers.
A URL does not identify the commissioned notary.
Correct. Keep the official information consistent.
The prescribed information remains required.

questions.stem: A Colorado RON session shows different versions of the record to the notary and signer. What must be confirmed?
options: That both view the same record, with changes and attachments made in real time
questions.explanation: The recording requirements include the same-record confirmation and real-time changes.
feedback: Hardware ownership does not establish record identity.
Payment does not match records.
Titles can match while contents differ.
Correct. Resolve version divergence before completion.

questions.stem: A Colorado provider wants to use personal data collected for RON to generate marketing leads. What does Rule 5.4 provide?
options: This marketing use is prohibited and cannot be waived by consent
Every signed consent makes it permissible
Only the provider's pricing policy matters
The notary can sell it if no stamp is used
questions.explanation: Rule 5.4 excludes additional business or marketing use by the listed participants and affiliates.
feedback: Correct. The rule expressly addresses consent.
Consent does not waive this prohibition.
Vendor pricing does not govern the restriction.
Data's remote-transaction source remains relevant.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary's employer seeks remote-customer data for new business promotions. Which rule reaches the employer?
options: Only the customer's document title rule
Rule 5.4's prohibition includes the employer and relevant businesses
No rule applies outside the provider
questions.explanation: The rule includes the remote notary's employer or contracted business.
feedback: Document titles do not define marketing permissions.
Correct. The prohibition is not limited to providers.
Stamp shape is unrelated.
The rule expressly covers more actors.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary plans the same Document Authentication Number for several in-person electronic notarizations. What does Rule 2.2 require?
options: Any one number can be reused forever
A different DAN for each electronic notarization
questions.explanation: Rule 2.2.2(a) requires a different DAN for each electronic notarization.
feedback: Reuse contradicts the rule.
Email does not replace the assigned number.
Correct. Keep the method distinct from RON-provider requirements.
An invoice is not a DAN.

questions.stem: A Colorado notary stores assigned DANs in a shared file for any employee to use. What duty applies?
options: The numbers are public office supplies
Secure them against another person's access or use
questions.explanation: The rule requires reasonable measures protecting assigned DANs and prohibits permitting others' access or use.
feedback: A file name does not secure access.
Employer consent cannot waive the rule.
They are controlled official authentication numbers.
Correct. Maintain individual security.

questions.stem: A Colorado electronic signer has not adopted the proposed electronic mark as a signature. What must the notary verify?
options: That the signer adopts it to function as their signature
questions.explanation: Rule 2.2.3 requires verifying the signer's adoption of the electronic signature.
feedback: Correct. Intent to sign is part of this electronic process.
File size does not establish adoption.
Revenue is unrelated.
An address cannot establish signing intent.

questions.stem: A Colorado electronic notary has no state approval for electronic capability but uses assigned-looking numbers created privately. What is required?
options: State notice of intent and approval before electronic work
questions.explanation: Rule 2.2.1 requires state approval, and authentication numbers come through the authorized process.
feedback: A disclaimer cannot create official approval.
Correct. Follow the actual electronic authorization route.
A password does not confer public authority.
A subscription is not state approval.

cards.title: Current evidence
cards.front: How close to application must qualification occur?
cards.rule: New approved training and state examination must fall within ninety days before applying.
cards.boundary: Renewals have their own timely training requirement.
cards.mixup: Old experience does not renew an expired completion certificate.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rules 2.1.3–2.1.4

cards.title: State connection
cards.front: What connects an applicant to Colorado?
cards.rule: Residence or a Colorado place of employment or practice satisfies the stated connection.
cards.boundary: The connection must be real.
cards.mixup: A mailbox alone does not establish a place of practice.
cards.source: Colorado applying and renewing FAQs, Q1

cards.title: Legal names
cards.front: How should application names match identification?
cards.rule: Use the legal first and last names required by the rule.
cards.boundary: Include every surname appearing on the ID.
cards.mixup: Abbreviating a compound surname can break the match.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rule 2.1.1

cards.title: Notarized affirmation
cards.front: What declaration supports the application?
cards.rule: Submit the signed and notarized affirmation.
cards.boundary: Training and exam certificates are separate evidence.
cards.mixup: A payment receipt does not notarize the declaration.
cards.source: Colorado applying and renewing FAQs, Q2

cards.title: Approval point
cards.front: When does the four-year term begin?
cards.rule: The commission begins on the approval date.
cards.boundary: Obtain the required supplies before acting.
cards.mixup: Course registration does not start the term.
cards.source: Colorado applying and renewing FAQs, Q5–Q6

cards.title: Rejected filing
cards.front: What correction window follows rejection?
cards.rule: Correct and obtain approval within ninety days of payment.
cards.boundary: Otherwise start over and pay again.
cards.mixup: A correction attempt alone may not complete approval.
cards.source: Colorado applying and renewing FAQs, Q4

cards.title: Training sources
cards.front: Which classes receive credit?
cards.rule: Use the Secretary or an approved vendor/course provider.
cards.boundary: Commercial approval is not endorsement of other products.
cards.mixup: A general signing-agent badge is not automatically approved training.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rule 2.1.5

cards.title: Return after lapse
cards.front: What distinction matters for returning notaries?
cards.rule: Rule 1.9 classifies a lapse over thirty days as a new applicant for its rules.
cards.boundary: The portal FAQ directs former Colorado notaries through renewal filing.
cards.mixup: Training classification and portal route can answer different questions.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rule 1.9; applying FAQ Q8

cards.title: Ordinary ID features
cards.front: Which ordinary documentary features are listed?
cards.rule: Government ID has a photograph or signature and is current or expired one year or less.
cards.boundary: Remote identification has separate requirements.
cards.mixup: Do not import the remote both-feature rule into every paper act.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q6

cards.title: Credential timing
cards.front: How does the ordinary expiration allowance work?
cards.rule: The ordinary FAQ permits up to one year after expiry.
cards.boundary: A longer lapse needs another qualifying identity basis.
cards.mixup: Expiry and the card's other required features are separate tests.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q6

cards.title: Witness knowledge
cards.front: What must the ordinary credible witness know?
cards.rule: The witness personally knows the signer needing identity evidence.
cards.boundary: The witness also appears and provides the sworn written verification.
cards.mixup: Secondhand stories do not create personal knowledge.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q6

cards.title: Witness identification
cards.front: How can an unfamiliar ordinary witness be identified?
cards.rule: The notary may identify that witness using sufficient ID.
cards.boundary: Follow the complete credible-witness procedure.
cards.mixup: Unknown to the notary is not identical to unable to identify.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q6

cards.title: Communication result
cards.front: What must the notary achieve with the signer?
cards.rule: Understand the signer and be understood by the signer.
cards.boundary: Use a qualifying interpreter arrangement when appropriate.
cards.mixup: A translated sign outside the office does not establish communication.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rule 2.3

cards.title: Interpreter presence
cards.front: Where does an in-person interpreter participate?
cards.rule: A human interpreter is in the same room for paper or in-person electronic acts.
cards.boundary: Remote interpreters use the approved platform's audio-video.
cards.mixup: A telephone-only substitute does not meet the stated route.
cards.source: Colorado Secretary of State interpreter FAQs, Q7

cards.title: Specialized credentials
cards.front: When does interpreter certification matter?
cards.rule: Deaf, hard-of-hearing and deafblind interpretation requires the specified accepted certification.
cards.boundary: Ordinary language interpreters do not generally apply to the SOS.
cards.mixup: Do not generalize one credential rule to every interpreter.
cards.source: Colorado Secretary of State interpreter FAQs, Q1–Q2

cards.title: Interpreter interests
cards.front: What can disqualify an interpreter?
cards.rule: Named or benefiting transaction roles and specified family interests are restricted.
cards.boundary: A real-estate agent's commission can create the stated problem.
cards.mixup: Language ability alone does not establish independence.
cards.source: Colorado Secretary of State interpreter FAQs, Q5–Q6

cards.title: Free participation
cards.front: What should identity checking be followed by?
cards.rule: Confirm knowing and willing participation in the transaction.
cards.boundary: A genuine ID cannot resolve coercion by itself.
cards.mixup: The companion's urgency is not the signer's free choice.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q1

cards.title: Earlier signatures
cards.front: What does a current acknowledgment establish?
cards.rule: The identified appearing signer acknowledges the signature as their own.
cards.boundary: The signature may have been made earlier.
cards.mixup: Do not claim to witness an earlier signing that was unseen.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q3

cards.title: Signature witnessing
cards.front: How does witnessing differ from acknowledgment?
cards.rule: The notary watches the identified signer sign.
cards.boundary: Certificate wording must match the procedure.
cards.mixup: An earlier signature cannot become witnessed through relabeling.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q4

cards.title: Oath or affirmation
cards.front: What distinguishes the two pledges?
cards.rule: An oath invokes a supreme being, while an affirmation is made under penalty of perjury.
cards.boundary: Both are solemn truth declarations.
cards.mixup: The stamp alone does not administer either pledge.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q2

cards.title: Actual certificate date
cards.front: Which date belongs in the certificate?
cards.rule: Use the real date of the notarial act.
cards.boundary: The FAQ forbids pre- or post-dating.
cards.mixup: A shipping deadline cannot supply a date exception.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q8

cards.title: Certificate corrections
cards.front: Who changes which part?
cards.rule: The signer changes the document, while the notary corrects the certificate.
cards.boundary: The FAQ describes visible correction, initials and date.
cards.mixup: A courier cannot rewrite the official certificate for convenience.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q19

cards.title: Undated documents
cards.front: Can an undated document be notarized?
cards.rule: The FAQ permits it if otherwise proper, with an undated-record journal note.
cards.boundary: An unused date blank must be completed or marked appropriately.
cards.mixup: No printed date differs from an unfilled blank.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q14 and Q16

cards.title: Copied signatures
cards.front: Can a faxed signature be acknowledged?
cards.rule: The original signer can appear and acknowledge the copied signature under the FAQ.
cards.boundary: This does not claim witnessing the original execution.
cards.mixup: Copying the signature does not supply the signer's appearance.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q15

cards.title: Relative interests
cards.front: Which relatives are included in conflict screening?
cards.rule: The FAQ lists spouse/civil-union partner, ancestors, descendants and siblings including half/step siblings.
cards.boundary: Apply the stated record-interest conditions.
cards.mixup: Certifying only another party's signature does not necessarily remove the conflict.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q18

cards.title: Official copy boundaries
cards.front: Which copies need a custodian route?
cards.rule: Records obtainable from the listed Colorado public offices are excluded from ordinary copy certification.
cards.boundary: The FAQ separately addresses federal and other-state copies.
cards.mixup: Another state's vital record is not treated identically to every Colorado vital record.
cards.source: Colorado powers and duties FAQs, Q13

cards.title: Contemporaneous entry
cards.front: When is the journal information recorded?
cards.rule: Record it at the time of notarization.
cards.boundary: Do not reconstruct routine entries weeks later.
cards.mixup: Monthly totals do not identify each act.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q8

cards.title: Every participant
cards.front: What happens with two simultaneous signers?
cards.rule: Use separate journal entries for each signer.
cards.boundary: Their names may share a certificate if they appear together.
cards.mixup: A shared certificate does not merge journal records.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q11

cards.title: Actual identity route
cards.front: How is identity recorded?
cards.rule: State personal knowledge or describe the satisfactory-evidence method and ID type actually used.
cards.boundary: Credible-witness acts are also recorded.
cards.mixup: Do not invent a credential for a personally known signer.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q8

cards.title: Employer-record exception
cards.front: When can the exception apply?
cards.rule: The retained original, copy or electronic record contains all required journal information.
cards.boundary: The firm or employer keeps that complete record.
cards.mixup: Any partial office photocopy does not automatically qualify.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q7

cards.title: Remote electronic journal
cards.front: What additional format applies to RON?
cards.rule: Use a compliant tamper-evident electronic journal unless the statutory exception applies.
cards.boundary: Identify the remote provider.
cards.mixup: A paper journal does not automatically meet the remote format.
cards.source: Colorado remote notarization FAQs, Q7

cards.title: Storage choice
cards.front: How can a completed journal be handled?
cards.rule: Choose personal ten-year retention, State Archives or the permitted employer arrangement and notify the state.
cards.boundary: Employer storage has its own continuing conditions.
cards.mixup: Finishing a book does not permit immediate disposal.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q9

cards.title: Employer custodian
cards.front: What duties follow authorized employer custody?
cards.rule: Protect the journal and comply with the specified copy, audit, officer-access and loss-notice duties.
cards.boundary: Rule 4.1 requires electronic notice within thirty days.
cards.mixup: Custody does not eliminate public-record responsibilities.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rules 4.1–4.3

cards.title: Loss reporting
cards.front: What deadline follows discovering a missing journal or stamp?
cards.rule: Notify the state within thirty days of discovery.
cards.boundary: Unauthorized employer retention can be reported as loss/theft.
cards.mixup: Waiting for renewal can miss the deadline.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q10

cards.title: Stamp shape
cards.front: What official device does Colorado require?
cards.rule: Use a rectangular ink stamp with a rectangular outline or border.
cards.boundary: Plain or decorative borders are allowed.
cards.mixup: An embosser does not replace the Colorado stamp.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q4

cards.title: Required content
cards.front: What belongs inside the stamp border?
cards.rule: Use the commissioned name, office/state wording, notary ID and expiration.
cards.boundary: No other information goes inside.
cards.mixup: Advertising slogans do not belong in the official border.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q4

cards.title: Old stamp
cards.front: What happens upon renewal or resignation?
cards.rule: Render the old stamp unusable.
cards.boundary: Use accurate current supplies after renewal.
cards.mixup: Remaining ink does not preserve expired commission information.
cards.source: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs, Q6

cards.title: Cap components
cards.front: What does the ordinary $15 maximum include?
cards.rule: The document notarization includes identity evidence, applicable oath and official certificate completion.
cards.boundary: Electronic/remote maximum is separately $25.
cards.mixup: Splitting an ID-check surcharge does not erase included components.
cards.source: Colorado fees FAQs, Q1

cards.title: Two transparency stages
cards.front: What fee communication is required?
cards.rule: Explain charges before the act and provide the required written listing.
cards.boundary: Apply the stated exceptions only when their conditions fit.
cards.mixup: An oral quote alone does not replace a required written record.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rule 2.4

cards.title: Employee exception
cards.front: Who may use the title-service documentation exception?
cards.rule: The specified title-company employee performing the listed qualifying services.
cards.boundary: Independent contractors have separate responsibilities.
cards.mixup: Serving a title company does not automatically make someone its employee.
cards.source: Colorado fees FAQs, Q2 and Q5

cards.title: Zero charges
cards.front: What if all services are free?
cards.rule: The FAQ requires no fee documentation for entirely free services.
cards.boundary: Charged associated services can still need documentation.
cards.mixup: Zero notarial price does not hide a charged travel amount.
cards.source: Colorado fees FAQs, Q7–Q8

cards.title: Customer identity
cards.front: Who receives the fee documentation?
cards.rule: The customer is the person signing the document.
cards.boundary: Use an acceptable actual fee record.
cards.mixup: Telling only a closing company does not automatically inform the signer.
cards.source: Colorado fees FAQs, Q9

cards.title: Separate approval
cards.front: What authority precedes Colorado RON?
cards.rule: Hold active ordinary status and obtain remote approval after the required training and exam.
cards.boundary: Filing intent early does not authorize immediate remote acts.
cards.mixup: A webcam subscription is not state approval.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rule 5.2.1

cards.title: Real-time method
cards.front: What appearance does RON require?
cards.rule: Use approved simultaneous audio-video communication and record the whole interaction.
cards.boundary: A prerecorded signing video is insufficient.
cards.mixup: A clear recorded image cannot supply live interaction.
cards.source: Colorado remote notarization FAQs, Q6

cards.title: Recording consent
cards.front: What must precede recording?
cards.rule: Explain the recording and storage details and obtain express verbal agreement.
cards.boundary: Refusal prevents the remote act.
cards.mixup: Silence is not the stated express consent.
cards.source: Colorado remote notarization FAQs, Q13

cards.title: Ten-year archive
cards.front: How long is the RON recording securely stored?
cards.rule: The FAQ requires ten years.
cards.boundary: Recording and journal obligations are distinct.
cards.mixup: The ordinary commission's term does not shorten retention.
cards.source: Colorado remote notarization FAQs, Q7 and Q12

cards.title: Foreign signer
cards.front: What adds conditions outside the United States?
cards.rule: The record needs the specified US connection and no actual known local prohibition.
cards.boundary: The notary still remains physically in Colorado.
cards.mixup: A US property connection does not waive the second condition.
cards.source: Colorado remote notarization FAQs, Q19

cards.title: Document exclusions
cards.front: Which records need special RON screening?
cards.rule: Electoral-process records are excluded and wills/codicils have special statutory restrictions.
cards.boundary: Qualifying real-estate RON is permitted but optional.
cards.mixup: General electronic capability does not authorize every document.
cards.source: Colorado remote notarization FAQs, Q9–Q11

cards.title: DAN control
cards.front: What applies to in-person electronic authentication numbers?
cards.rule: Use a different DAN for each electronic notarization and secure it against others' use.
cards.boundary: Follow the electronic notice/approval process.
cards.mixup: A shared office list does not establish individual control.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rule 2.2

cards.title: Transaction data
cards.front: May RON personal data become marketing leads?
cards.rule: Rule 5.4 prohibits the stated additional-business and marketing use.
cards.boundary: The restriction includes the notary, employer and provider/affiliates.
cards.mixup: Customer consent does not waive this prohibition.
cards.source: Colorado Notary Program Rules, 8 CCR 1505-11, Rule 5.4

commission.summary: Align Colorado eligibility, timely approved training, the state examination and complete online application evidence.

sections.heading: Qualify and document the application
sections.body: The applying FAQ requires the listed age, lawful-presence, Colorado-connection, English-literacy and character conditions. Residence or a Colorado place of employment or practice supplies the state connection. Rule 2.1 requires legal-name consistency, online filing, approved training and the Secretary's examination. The notarized affirmation, acceptable application ID and separate training and examination certificates support the filing. Application identification requirements serve a different purpose from identifying a customer for a notarial act.

sections.heading: Keep time windows distinct
sections.body: New training and examination occur within ninety days before application. Renewal training and examination have their own ninety-day window. Rule 1.9 classifies certain expired commissions as new applicants for the rules, while the portal FAQ directs former Colorado notaries through the renewal filing route. A rejected application must be corrected and approved within ninety days of payment. State approval begins the four-year term, and required supplies must be ready before acts are performed.

example.heading: Worked example — a returning office worker
example.body: A former Colorado notary returns to administrative work after a lengthy lapse. The worker follows the portal's returning-notary renewal instructions and meets the applicable new-applicant training classification under Rule 1.9. Current training and exam certificates, the notarized affirmation and ID are prepared before filing. Possession of the old stamp does not restore the expired office.

keyFacts: Approved training and state examination are separate evidence.
The ordinary completion window is ninety days before filing.
A receipt is distinct from approval and active authority.

identification.summary: Choose the identity and communication route that matches the actual Colorado appointment, including qualifying witnesses and interpreters.

sections.heading: Ordinary evidence and witnesses
sections.body: The powers FAQ describes ordinary government ID that is current or expired one year or less and contains a photograph or signature. The credible-witness route requires a personally appearing witness who personally knows the signer and provides the sworn written verification. The notary either knows the witness or identifies the witness through sufficient ID. Record the actual identity method. Remote identification follows separate conditions and should not be assembled from whichever ordinary rules seem convenient.

sections.heading: Communication and interpreter safeguards
sections.body: Rule 2.3 requires mutual understanding between signer and notary. The interpreter FAQ requires a human interpreter, in-room presence for paper and in-person electronic acts, and approved-platform audio-video presence for remote acts. Specialized deaf, hard-of-hearing and deafblind interpretation uses the stated accepted credentials. Review transaction and family interests and record required interpreter details. Identity evidence does not independently establish understanding or free participation.

example.heading: Worked example — an interpreted appointment
example.body: A customer brings a real-estate agent as interpreter for a record naming and benefiting that agent. The language skill does not remove the FAQ's interpreter-interest restriction. Arrange a qualifying human interpreter through the proper presence method, establish the customer's identity and voluntary participation, and record interpreter details before completing a truthful certificate.

keyFacts: Ordinary ID and RON identification have different conditions.
A credible witness personally knows the signer.
Interpreter presence, interests and credentials require separate checks.

acknowledgments.summary: Match Colorado certificate wording to the actual act, participation, document condition and officer's impartiality.

sections.heading: Distinguish the acts
sections.body: An acknowledgment permits the appearing identified signer to acknowledge an earlier signature. Signature witnessing requires the notary to watch execution. A verification requires the actual signing and oath or affirmation described by the certificate. A journal signature cannot supply a missing document signature. Read each certificate field to distinguish the notary from the appearing signer, and complete the required English certificate with the true venue and date.

sections.heading: Screen the record and conflicts
sections.body: The powers FAQ prohibits pre- and post-dating and assigns document changes to the signer and certificate corrections to the notary. Resolve unfilled blanks using the stated signer-completion process. An undated document without a date blank can be distinguished in the journal. Screen self and specified-relative interests and the special copy-certification exclusions for Colorado public-custodian records. An admonishment identifies incorrect practice that should be reviewed and corrected, and repeated warnings may prompt investigation.

example.heading: Worked example — a faxed earlier signature
example.body: A Colorado customer appears with a fax bearing their earlier signature. The FAQ permits an acknowledgment of that signature under the appearance conditions. The notary identifies the customer, takes the actual acknowledgment and dates the certificate for today's act. The notary does not claim to have witnessed the earlier original signing.

keyFacts: Acknowledgment and witnessing have different execution requirements.
Certificate date and venue describe the actual act.
A party or qualifying relative interest can disqualify the notary.

journals.summary: Make complete contemporary Colorado records, apply the employer-record exception precisely and preserve completed journals through an allowed route.

sections.heading: Record the actual act and people
sections.body: The stamps-and-journals FAQ requires journal recording at the act, including date and time, act and document description, participant names and addresses, signatures, identity method and fee. Multiple signers receive separate entries even when a simultaneous appearance shares a certificate. Oral oaths are included. Interpreter and remote-provider information belong in applicable entries. The employer-record exception depends on the retained record containing every required element.

sections.heading: Choose and report continuing custody
sections.body: Completed journals may follow personal ten-year retention, State Archives or the permitted employer-custody arrangement with required notice. Rule 4.1 requires the employer-disposition form within thirty days and a copy to the employer. Custody carries security, lawful-copy, state-audit, peace-officer and loss-notification responsibilities. The FAQ requires reporting a discovered journal or stamp loss within thirty days. Remote acts additionally use a compliant tamper-evident electronic journal unless the statutory exception applies.

example.heading: Worked example — a firm retains records
example.body: A Colorado firm keeps document copies but omits the witnesses' addresses and identity details. Those copies do not satisfy the complete-information exception. The notary maintains full entries. Later, if a completed journal is properly left with the employer, the notary files the disposition notice and provides its copy, and the employer assumes the stated custodial duties.

keyFacts: Journal timing is contemporaneous with the act.
Employer retention has specific content, notice and custody conditions.

seals-fees.summary: Use accurate Colorado equipment and apply current fee caps together with disclosure, documentation and role-specific exceptions.

sections.heading: Official stamp and signature
sections.body: Colorado requires a rectangular ink stamp with a rectangular border. The border may be plain or decorative and contains the exact commissioned name, required office and state wording, ID and expiration. No other information belongs inside. The FAQ specifies no particular stamp size or ink color but rejects embossers. Keep the certificate legible, use the official signature on record and render obsolete stamps unusable on renewal or resignation.

sections.heading: Charge and disclose the actual service
sections.body: The current FAQ lists a $15 ordinary per-document maximum and $25 electronic or remote maximum. Required identity, applicable oath and official completion are included in the ordinary service. Additional service charges require the stated advance information and written itemization. Apply the narrow title-company employee exception to the correct role. Contractors document their own charges. Entirely free services and zero notarial prices with associated charges have distinct FAQ treatment.

example.heading: Worked example — a mobile invoice
example.body: A Colorado mobile notary quotes the ordinary notarial amount and a separately identified travel service before acting. The written record clearly identifies the notary's actual charges and is supplied to the signer. Scheduling through a website does not turn the paper act into an electronic act. The notary uses the ordinary cap and a current compliant stamp.

keyFacts: The official stamp is rectangular ink with required content only.
Current listed caps are $15 ordinary and $25 electronic/remote.
Advance charge information and written documentation are separate requirements.

electronic-ron.summary: Maintain Colorado's separate electronic and remote authorizations, approved technology, identity process and continuing evidence.

sections.heading: Approval and the actual method
sections.body: Rule 2.2 addresses in-person electronic approval and unique Document Authentication Numbers. Secure DANs against others' use and verify the signer's adoption of the electronic signature. RON follows separate active-status, training, examination and approval requirements under Rule 5.2.1. Use an approved provider and keep at least one on record. Remote renewal has its own timely training, exam and fee. A provider subscription does not supply public authorization.

sections.heading: Remote participation and safeguards
sections.body: The notary remains physically in Colorado. A signer outside the US triggers the stated US-connection and no-actual-known-prohibition conditions. Screen electoral-process exclusions and special will restrictions. Obtain express recording/storage consent and record the entire live interaction for secure ten-year storage. Complete the required identity route and certificate, including interpreter details where applicable. Rule 5.4 prohibits the listed use of remote personal data for additional business or marketing, even with consent.

example.heading: Worked example — an overseas property owner
example.body: A signer abroad wants a Colorado remote act involving US property. The approved notary remains in Colorado, checks the outside-US conditions, obtains express consent after recording/storage disclosure and conducts the full approved live identity and signing process. The certificate states audio-video use and the electronic journal identifies the provider. The property connection does not remove the other conditions.

keyFacts: RON requires separate state approval and approved providers.
The notary stays physically in Colorado.
Recording retention and electronic journal requirements are distinct.

articles.title: Qualifying interpreters at Colorado closings
articles.description: Apply interpreter presence, qualification, conflict and recording requirements to an actual closing.
articles.lede: A Boulder customer needs interpretation during a closing. The customer's real-estate agent offers to interpret, but the agent is named in the record and will receive the transaction commission.

sections.heading: Separate language skill from eligibility
sections.body: The Colorado interpreter FAQ does not treat language ability as the entire qualification. A named or transaction-benefiting real-estate agent has the stated disqualifying interest. Before starting the act, arrange an interpreter who meets the applicable conditions. The agent's familiarity with the customer cannot remove the transaction role.

sections.heading: Choose the correct presence method
sections.body: The interpreter must be a human being. For paper and in-person electronic acts, the FAQ requires the interpreter in the room with the notary and signer. For RON, the interpreter appears through audio-video technology on the approved provider platform. A telephone-only substitute or translation application does not satisfy those stated arrangements.

sections.heading: Check specialized credentials and interests
sections.body: The FAQ distinguishes ordinary language interpreters from services for deaf, hard-of-hearing and deafblind participants, for whom the specified accepted credentials apply. It also addresses specified family-related interests. Evaluate the interpreter's actual relationship and role instead of assuming that a friend or relative is automatically a suitable independent communication channel.

sections.heading: Preserve participation details
sections.body: The journal identifies the interpreter's full name, address and credential or certification number if any. In-person certificate identification is recommended, while remote certificate identification is required as specified. At the Boulder closing, these records should reflect the qualifying interpreter who actually participated and the actual authorized appearance method.

sources.title: Colorado Secretary of State interpreter FAQs

faqs.q: Must interpreters apply to the Secretary of State?
faqs.a: The FAQ says no general interpreter application is required.

faqs.q: Can an app replace the interpreter?
faqs.a: The FAQ requires a human interpreter through the stated presence method.

articles.title: Does an office file replace a Colorado notary journal?
articles.description: Test employer-retained records against the full journal-information requirement.
articles.h1: Does an office file replace a Colorado notary journal?
articles.lede: A Colorado credit union retains signed document scans and assumes its employee needs no notary journal. The scans contain names and signatures but omit identity methods, addresses and fees.

sections.heading: Test the entire exception
sections.body: The official stamps-and-journals FAQ recognizes an exception when the original, copy or electronic record contains every required journal element and the firm or employer keeps it. The word every matters. An ordinary office scan does not qualify simply because it proves a document exists or shows a signature.

sections.heading: Compare the missing fields
sections.body: The required information includes the act's date and time, act and record description, participant names and addresses, signatures, identity basis and fee. Add interpreter and remote-provider information where applicable. The credit union's document scans should be compared against this full list before relying on the exception.

sections.heading: Preserve separate signer records
sections.body: The FAQ permits multiple simultaneous signers on one certificate but calls for separate journal entries for each signer. That rule makes participant-level records important. The person who pays the charge does not replace the other appearing signers. A combined office appointment label may fail to show the required information about each act.

sections.heading: Distinguish later custody
sections.body: The employer-record exception concerns how current acts are documented. Leaving a completed journal with an employer is a separate disposition route with notice and continuing duties. At the credit union, an incomplete scan practice should be corrected by maintaining compliant records. It should not be justified by a future agreement to store old books.

sources.title: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs

faqs.q: Does any retained photocopy qualify?
faqs.a: The retained record must contain all required journal information.

faqs.q: Is the completed-journal employer route the same exception?
faqs.a: It is a separate custody and disposition arrangement with its own requirements.

articles.intent: Plan lawful completed-journal custody and notification
articles.title: After a Colorado journal is full
articles.description: Choose personal retention, State Archives or qualifying employer custody and complete the required notice.
articles.h1: After a Colorado journal is full
articles.lede: A Colorado law office employee finishes a notarial journal while preparing to leave the firm. The final page does not end the record's legal life.

sections.heading: Choose an allowed destination
sections.body: The stamps-and-journals FAQ describes personal retention for ten years from the last entry, submission to State Archives or the permitted employer arrangement. The state must be notified of the selected route. Use the official completed-journal form and preserve the details needed to locate the record later.

sections.heading: Complete employer notice
sections.body: If the notary leaves the journal with the firm under the authorized route, Rule 4.1 calls for electronic state submission within thirty days and a copy to the firm at submission. The employer agrees to the continuing retention or archive route. An informal desk handover does not document these obligations.

sections.heading: Recognize the custodian's duties
sections.body: Rule 4.2 requires the employer custodian to secure the journal and comply with the specified transaction-copy, state-audit, peace-officer and loss-notification duties. The employer can retain indefinitely or transmit to State Archives with the required notice under Rule 4.3. Custody does not make the record an unrestricted marketing database.

sections.heading: Handle unauthorized retention separately
sections.body: The FAQ says an employer retaining the journal without permission may be reported as a loss or theft. It gives a thirty-day discovery-based notification period for a missing journal or stamp and an official report-loss account action. The departing employee should distinguish this problem from a properly documented voluntary custody arrangement.

sources.title: Colorado official stamps and journals FAQs

faqs.q: When does personal retention start?
faqs.a: The FAQ measures ten years from the last journal entry.

faqs.q: Does authorized employer custody remove security duties?
faqs.a: Rule 4.2 assigns the custodian continuing protection and access responsibilities.

articles.intent: Apply caps and document actual charged services
articles.title: A clear Colorado notarial invoice
articles.description: Separate the act cap, associated charges, advance disclosure and written documentation.
articles.lede: A Colorado mobile contractor schedules a paper closing online, performs the appointment in person and bills a notarial amount plus travel. Online booking does not determine the notarial method.

sections.heading: Choose the act category
sections.body: The current official fee FAQ lists $15 per ordinary document and $25 for electronic or remote notarization. Required identity evidence, applicable oath or affirmation and signature/certificate/stamp completion are included in the ordinary act. Separate labels for these components cannot make the same ordinary service escape its cap.

sections.heading: Explain actual charges first
sections.body: Additional services such as travel, mileage or copying must receive the stated separate itemization and advance information. Rule 2.4 permits verbal or written information before the act, followed by the required written listing. The mobile contractor should explain the actual proposed amounts while the customer can decide about the service.

sections.heading: Document the signer-facing transaction
sections.body: The FAQ defines the customer as the signer. A receipt, itemized invoice, closing statement, transaction summary or another accepted record can identify the applicable charges. A contractor documents the contractor's own fee rather than guessing what a closing company ultimately charged. A required document should be delivered within the stated timing.

sections.heading: Apply exceptions to the actual role
sections.body: The defined title-company employee exception does not automatically include an independent contractor serving that company. Entirely free services have different documentation treatment, while a zero notarial charge with a charged associated service can still need a record. Read the applicable FAQ conditions before using an exception for the mobile invoice.

faqs.q: Does online booking permit the remote fee cap?
faqs.a: The category follows the actual notarization method, not appointment scheduling.

faqs.q: Is a verbal quote always enough?
faqs.a: Nonexempt charged services also need the required written documentation.

articles.intent: Complete actual dates and apply the proper correction roles
articles.title: Correct the Colorado certificate you actually performed
articles.description: Keep act date, signer fields and certificate corrections truthful.
articles.h1: Correct the Colorado certificate you actually performed
articles.lede: A Colorado package contains yesterday's drafting date, an unused certificate date and a mistake in the customer's street address. The notary must distinguish the document from the official certificate.

sections.heading: Use the real act date
sections.body: The powers FAQ prohibits pre- and post-dating a certificate without exceptions. Drafting, shipping and notarial dates can differ. When the signer appears today, the actual completed act is dated today. A recipient's deadline cannot turn yesterday into the true date of an event that occurred now.

sections.heading: Identify the correct participant
sections.body: The common-mistakes page warns against inserting the notary's name where the certificate identifies the appearing customer. Read each field's role. The notary's official name and signature have their own places. The certificate also needs the actual venue, act type, stamp, title and exact commission expiration information.

sections.heading: Separate correction authority
sections.body: Only the signer changes the underlying document. Only the notary corrects the notarial certificate. The FAQ describes lining through the error in ink, adding the correction above or beside it and initialing and dating the correction. This preserves a visible record instead of silently erasing the original information.

sections.heading: Resolve the packet's two issues
sections.body: The signer handles the address error in the document using the proper document process. The notary fills the actual certificate date and corrects any certificate error through the stated method. A journal signature cannot substitute for a document signing that the certificate claims occurred. Every statement should describe the actual completed procedure.

sources.title: Colorado Secretary of State common mistakes FAQs

faqs.q: Can a courier choose a backdated certificate?
faqs.a: The FAQ requires the actual notarial date and states no pre- or post-dating exception.

faqs.q: Who may correct the certificate?
faqs.a: The notary makes the certificate correction. The signer controls changes to the document.

articles.intent: Distinguish acknowledgment from witnessing on earlier signatures
articles.title: Acknowledge an earlier signature in Colorado
articles.description: Apply the acknowledgment procedure without falsely claiming to witness past signing.
articles.h1: Acknowledge an earlier signature in Colorado
articles.lede: A Colorado customer has only a faxed copy of an agreement signed earlier. The customer appears personally and wants the signature acknowledged for the recipient.

sections.heading: Identify what acknowledgment establishes
sections.body: The powers FAQ describes acknowledgment through the identified signer's appearance and confirmation that the signature is theirs. The signature need not have been made before the notary. This flexibility concerns the act's execution history. It does not eliminate today's identification, appearance, journal or certificate requirements.

sections.heading: Avoid a false witnessing statement
sections.body: Signature witnessing describes watching the signer sign. A certificate saying signed before me should not be used to claim that the notary observed an earlier event elsewhere. An acknowledgment can truthfully describe the present acknowledgment of that signature. Match the certificate to the actual permitted act instead of selecting the most convenient label.

sections.heading: Apply the fax-copy guidance
sections.body: The FAQ expressly permits the original signer to acknowledge a photocopied or faxed signature when the stated conditions are met. The copy's presence alone is insufficient. The person responsible for the original signature participates and acknowledges it. A courier who merely delivers the fax does not become that signer.

sections.heading: Record today's event
sections.body: At the appointment, establish the actual signer's identity and participation, take the acknowledgment and use today's act date and actual Colorado venue. The journal can identify the faxed record and procedure. The certificate does not guarantee the agreement's contents or claim witnessing of its original signing.

sources.title: Colorado Secretary of State common mistakes FAQs

faqs.q: Must every acknowledgment signature be made before the notary?
faqs.a: The FAQ permits acknowledgment of an earlier signature.

faqs.q: Does the fax itself supply the appearance?
faqs.a: The original signer still appears and makes the required acknowledgment.

articles.keyword: Colorado notary certify copy vital records
articles.intent: Distinguish Colorado custodian records from other-state or federal records
articles.title: Which records can a Colorado notary copy-certify?
articles.description: Apply the official record-custodian exclusion and the separate other-jurisdiction guidance.
articles.h1: Which records can a Colorado notary copy-certify?
articles.lede: A Colorado desk receives a local birth certificate, an out-of-state marriage record and a federal record bearing a copying restriction. Their government origin does not produce one uniform answer.

sections.heading: Check the Colorado custodian exclusion
sections.body: The powers FAQ excludes certification of copies obtainable from Colorado's clerk and recorder, Secretary of State, State Archives or vital-records office. A Colorado birth or marriage record should be screened through that custodian rule. A private customer's consent does not grant the notary authority that the exclusion removes.

sections.heading: Read the other-state distinction
sections.body: The FAQ separately permits copies of other-state vital records, including the listed birth, death, marriage and divorce examples. Do not import the Colorado-custodian exclusion into a blanket prohibition for every other jurisdiction's record. Identify the original record and apply the exact condition governing that source.

sections.heading: Observe a face-of-record prohibition
sections.body: Permission for federal or other-state copies is conditioned on the record not stating on its face that copying is illegal. The federal record's restriction therefore matters independently of customer urgency or the cost of obtaining another copy. A high-quality scanner cannot resolve a legal copying restriction.

sections.heading: Keep the act within its actual scope
sections.body: For the three desk requests, direct the local record to its official custodian, evaluate the out-of-state record under the permitted route and respect the federal record's restriction. Complete only an authorized accurate-copy act with the required certificate and journal record. A copy certificate should not become an unrelated legal opinion.

faqs.q: Are all out-of-state vital records treated like Colorado records?
faqs.a: The FAQ expressly distinguishes other-state vital-record copies.

faqs.q: Can customer consent remove a printed copying prohibition?
faqs.a: The published permission depends on absence of that face-of-record restriction.

articles.keyword: Colorado remote notary outside United States
articles.intent: Apply geography, nexus and prohibition conditions to foreign signers
articles.title: A Colorado RON appointment with an overseas signer
articles.description: Check both the notary's physical location and the foreign signer's record conditions.
articles.h1: A Colorado RON appointment with an overseas signer
articles.lede: A property owner temporarily abroad requests a remote act involving a US property transaction. The commissioned notary is considering taking the appointment while traveling outside Colorado.

sections.heading: Locate the officer first
sections.body: The remote FAQ requires the Colorado notary to remain physically within Colorado. An office address, active subscription or Colorado customer does not substitute for actual location. The traveling notary must satisfy that territory condition before considering the overseas signer's separate eligibility. Geography applies to the official actor as well as the customer.

sections.heading: Establish the specified US connection
sections.body: For a signer outside the US, the electronic record must relate to the listed US matter, US property or substantially connected US transaction. Identify that connection from the actual request. The property owner's US transaction may supply it, but a completely unrelated foreign matter cannot be assumed eligible under the same wording.

sections.heading: Check the second foreign condition
sections.body: The notary must not actually know that the act is prohibited where the signer is physically located. The US connection and no-actual-known-prohibition condition are cumulative. A customer's promise to waive another jurisdiction's restriction does not change what the notary actually knows. Resolve the stated conditions before conducting the session.

sections.heading: Complete every remote safeguard
sections.body: Once geography and subject conditions fit, the approved notary still follows the live provider, identification, recording-consent, certificate and electronic-journal process. The US property connection does not authorize a prerecorded act or remove ten-year recording retention. Document the actual provider and method, with all required participant statements.

faqs.q: Can the notary conduct Colorado RON while physically abroad?
faqs.a: The FAQ requires the notary to be physically in Colorado.

faqs.q: Does US property automatically resolve every overseas condition?
faqs.a: The separate actual-known-prohibition condition and all ordinary RON safeguards remain applicable.

articles.intent: Plan disclosure, express consent and complete remote evidence
articles.title: Record a Colorado remote act with informed participation
articles.description: Obtain express recording/storage consent and preserve the complete live act.
articles.h1: Record a Colorado remote act with informed participation
articles.lede: A Colorado remote signer agrees to video but asks that the provider stop recording during identity checks. The notary needs a complete authorized procedure rather than selected excerpts.

sections.heading: Explain recording before obtaining consent
sections.body: The remote FAQ requires telling the signer that the notarization will be recorded and explaining where and for how long the recording will be stored. Obtain express verbal agreement to both recording and storage. Silence or a provider's general advertisement does not supply the stated participant consent.

sections.heading: Record the full live interaction
sections.body: The FAQ requires real-time sight-and-sound communication and recording of the entire interaction. A previously filmed signing video cannot be notarized as the current live act. Stopping the recording for a required part of the procedure would leave the evidence incomplete. A screenshot of the final seal cannot replace the record.

sections.heading: Include the identity explanations
sections.body: The recorded content includes the notary, time, records, signer and applicable witness information. Personal knowledge needs an explanation of how and for how long the signer is known. A credible witness supplies the stated knowledge explanation. Credential-based identity follows the complete remote presentation, analysis and additional-method route.

sections.heading: Preserve both evidence streams
sections.body: The recording is securely stored for ten years. The remote journal separately identifies the provider and uses the compliant electronic format unless the statutory exception applies. If the signer refuses the recording arrangement, the FAQ says the remote act cannot proceed. Explain an appropriate lawful service route instead of silently omitting evidence.

faqs.q: Can the signer opt out of recording while continuing RON?
faqs.a: The FAQ says the notary cannot perform the remote act if the signer refuses recording.

faqs.q: Does a video archive replace the electronic journal?
faqs.a: The FAQ addresses the recording and compliant journal as separate requirements.

articles.intent: Distinguish in-person electronic authentication from remote capability
articles.title: Electronic documents and remote appearance in Colorado
articles.description: Understand DAN controls, electronic approval and the separate remote-notary process.
articles.h1: Electronic documents and remote appearance in Colorado
articles.lede: A Colorado office adopts electronic signatures for in-room appointments and then wants customers to connect remotely. The electronic record format and the remote appearance method require different checks.

sections.heading: Approve the in-person electronic capability
sections.body: Rule 2.2 requires the notice of intent and state approval before electronic notarization. It describes the electronic signature information and Document Authentication Numbers used with that method. An applicant may file intent early but cannot act before commissioning and approval. Privately invented numbers are not the authorized authentication process.

sections.heading: Control each authentication number
sections.body: The rule requires a different DAN for each electronic notarization and reasonable measures against another person's access or use. It also requires verifying that the signer adopted the electronic signature to function as their signature. A shared employee file of reusable numbers would undermine the individual official control described by the rule.

sections.heading: Add the separate remote route
sections.body: Moving the signer out of the room introduces the remote qualification, provider and live-communication requirements. An active ordinary commission, separate remote training/exam evidence and state approval precede remote work. At least one approved provider stays on record. Buying a video application does not complete that authorization.

sections.heading: Protect transaction information
sections.body: Rule 5.4 prohibits the listed additional-business and marketing use of RON personal information by the notary, relevant employer/business and provider affiliates. The rule says consent cannot waive that prohibition. The office's technology plan therefore must address identity, authentication, appearance, evidence storage and data use as separate responsibilities.

faqs.q: Can one DAN be reused for all electronic acts?
faqs.a: Rule 2.2.2 requires a different DAN for each electronic notarization.

faqs.q: Does a remote customer's consent permit marketing use of transaction data?
faqs.a: Rule 5.4 says the stated marketing prohibition cannot be waived by consent.
